name: Motion Principles
tagline: A blue ball bounces, stretches and leaves ghost trails while handwritten notes name every animation principle.
description: Clean motion-craft look: white and black scenes hard-cut against each other, one electric-blue element that squashes, stretches and leaves onion-skin ghosts, and handwritten notes with drawn arrows naming what's happening. The preview is a reel about animation principles starring a bouncing ball.

display.usage: Statements and name 200–300px, tracking -0.03em, all caps; can be scaled non-uniformly to show stretch

body.usage: Handwritten annotations 64–84px in blue (red for corrections), slightly rotated, written on left to right

mono.usage: Tiny uppercase labels 22–26px, tracking 0.16em, 50% opacity: axis names, easing values, frame rate

transitions: hard cut between white and black scenes, no fades or wipes
nothing is carried across a cut; each shot starts moving on its first frame
textAnimations: handwriting write-on: clip-path inset 100% → 0 on the right edge, linear, 0.3–0.45s
arrows: SVG path with pathLength=1000 and dasharray 1000, strokeDashoffset 1000 → 0 (GSAP rounds px values, so avoid pathLength=1), 0.15–0.3s, arrowhead drawn in the same path
giant word: scaleX 2.6 / scaleY 0.3 → 1 / 1.7 on elastic.out, 0.55s
final name rises from a clipped baseline on expo.out

rhythm.notes: Seven scenes of 0.7–2.2s. Every scene shows one principle moving plus one or two annotations that write on in the first half second. Last scene holds the longest.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- Palette: white #ffffff and ink #0a0a0a backgrounds that hard-cut against each other; one electric blue #2540ff (#6b82ff on black) for the moving element, a small red #ff3b30 only for corrections and emphasis.
- Animate the subject (or a simple stand-in shape for it) with textbook principles you can see: fall power2.in, rise power2.out, squash to ~1.6×0.5 for 0.09s on contact, stretch ~0.84×1.28 in the air, and thin blue outline copies stamped every 0.06s so the spacing shows.
- Annotate like a motion designer's notebook: Caveat 700 at 64–84px, rotated −4° to 3°, written on with a linear clip-path reveal and followed by a hand-drawn SVG arrow (pathLength 1000, dashoffset 1000→0, 0.2s). Use real terms ('anticipation', 'slow in, slow out', 'stagger: 45ms', 'follow-through').
- Tiny mono labels (22px, uppercase, tracking 0.16em, 50% opacity) carry the data: axis names, ease names, durations.
- Fake motion blur by stacking 10–15 copies delayed by 5ms with falling opacity, tweened on expo.out so they converge into a sharp shape; giant words snap in on elastic (scaleX 2.6 / scaleY 0.3 → 1).
- Optional motifs: a position-vs-time curve that draws while an object follows the same ease with ghost frames; a final name in Inter Tight 900 whose full stop drops as a bouncing ball.
- Hard cuts only, each shot moving from its first frame. Avoid gradients, glow, drop shadows, frames and decorative corner labels.
example: The preview is a motion designer's reel about animation principles: a blue ball squashing with onion-skin trails, a spacing graph, a progress ring and a name card whose full stop is the ball. Don't copy this scene unless asked.
